sentences.text: Aralazhdarcho bostobensis is the only known species of an azhdarchid pterosaur that lived in Kazakhstan during the Late Cretaceous. The name combines the Aral Sea and the genus Azhdarcho, while the species name refers to the Bostobe Formation.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of the front part of a neck vertebra, likely the fifth or sixth one.
Fossils of Aralazhdarcho were discovered in the Bostobe Formation at the Shakh-Shakh locality in Kazakhstan. The genus and species were formally named in 2007 by Alexander Averianov.
It is classified in the family Azhdarchidae because it lacks teeth and dates to the correct geological period. Averianov assigned it to Azhdarchidae based on its lack of teeth and geological age.

Some analyses place Aralazhdarcho in the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae alongside Phosphatodraco. Other studies suggest Aralazhdarcho belongs outside the Quetzalcoatlinae subfamily in a more basal position.
This pterosaur lived during the Santonian or early Campanian stages of the Late Cretaceous in Kazakhstan. The animal lived between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether the genus Samrukia is actually a junior synonym of Aralazhdarcho.
